newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says divided Israelis halt talks over Hebron.
newsitem.headline: PLO says divided Israelis halt talks over Hebron.

text.p: Palestinian and Israeli negotiators ended a meeting on Friday because of deep differences among members of the Israeli delegation, PLO officials said.

They said they spent hours waiting for the Israeli delegation to settle an internal dispute over issues that should have been agreed and drafted over a redeployment of Israeli troops from the West Bank town of Hebron.

"We came to Eilat with an agreement to start drafting a protocol on a Hebron deal after the major issues were resolved earlier," said a PLO (Palestine Liberation Organisation) official, who asked not to be identified.
"However, internal disputes of the Israeli delegation prevented any progress. They wanted the meetings to be postponed until next week."
PLO aide Hassan Asfour said: "When we find a serious negotiator we will have a serious agereement. They are not serious. We have wasted our time."
U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross said both sides would meet later on Friday. "They have narrowed the differences. They're working hard but there are still differences to be overcome," said Ross.
